extracted.intended_audience: writers (short fiction and poets) intending to submit to Asimov's Science Fiction
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and sending short fiction and poetry submissions to Asimov's Science Fiction magazine, including acceptable genres, length limits, formatting, rights, payment, and submission process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable short story length
rubrics_metrics.description: You can submit a short story between 1000-20,000 words for consideration without worrying about it being rejected. Any science fiction manuscript outside that range though, has a very small chance of being accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Asimov's is 'very flexible as to what constitutes a short story' but practical acceptance odds are highest within 1,000–20,000 words. If your manuscript is much longer and goes up to the allowable 20,000 words, you will be paid additional 8 cents per word up to the maximum.

rubrics_metrics.name: No serialized works
rubrics_metrics.description: Asimov’s science fiction magazine also does not accept serialized works.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not submit installments or parts of a serial; full standalone pieces only.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poetry length limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Poetry within the magazine’s acceptable genre is also accepted. Do make sure, however, that your poems do not exceed 40 lines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep individual poems to 40 lines or fewer to meet Asimov's stated limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preferred story focus and style
rubrics_metrics.description: This science fiction magazine predominantly favors character-oriented short stories and poetry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For the best chance of getting your work published on Asimov’s, ensure that your work is character oriented, with science as the backdrop of the story – a means to an end if you will.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable genre range (including borderline works)
rubrics_metrics.description: In addition to science fiction, work that qualifies as borderline fantasy, surreal fiction, and slipstream can also be published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions that sit near genre boundaries (slipstream, surreal, borderline fantasy) may be considered, provided they fit the magazine's overall character-oriented SF sensibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content restrictions (violence/sex)
rubrics_metrics.description: Excessive violence and sex however, is not acceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid depictions of graphic or gratuitous sexual content or extreme violence; such material reduces acceptance chances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment rates for fiction
rubrics_metrics.description: Should your science fiction manuscript make the cut, Asimov’s Science Fiction will pay you 8-10 cents per word for every word up to 7500 words. That’s $600-$750 in case you are counting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard pay: 8–10¢/word for words up to 7,500. If the manuscript is longer (up to 20,000), you will be paid an additional 8¢/word for the extra words up to the maximum (example numbers given in the article).

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment rates for poetry
rubrics_metrics.description: Payment for poetry is $1 per line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Poetry pay is calculated per line; ensure poem length (≤40 lines) to estimate payment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rights retained / granted
rubrics_metrics.description: In exchange for payment, you will be giving up the First English Language serial rights as well as certain non-exclusive rights to your science fiction work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should understand they grant first English-language serial rights and some non-exclusive rights when accepting payment; check Asimov's contract/terms for exact scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission method (online only) and file formats
rubrics_metrics.description: You can easily submit your science fiction manuscript online for consideration by Asimov’s magazine. Email submissions are a no-no. What you need to do is use the Online Submission System provided in order to submit your work. That work should be in the .doc; .docx, or .rtf formats.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the magazine's Online Submission System; do not send submissions via email. Prepare manuscript files in .doc, .docx, or .rtf before uploading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required submission metadata / materials
rubrics_metrics.description: In addition to your manuscript, you will need to submit your cover letter, name, email address, and story title among other things.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide author contact details and story title in the submission form. The cover letter is optional but fields for basic metadata are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover letter guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Your cover letter, while optional, is a great way to include your publishing history and length of the story. Otherwise, if you choose to exclude it, you should include your word count on the top right-hand first page of your manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you submit a cover letter, include relevant publishing history and story length. If no cover letter, place word count on the top right of the manuscript's first page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript tracking and inquiries
rubrics_metrics.description: Do make sure that you take note of your manuscript tracking number, which will be sent to your confirmation email. Wait for 5 weeks to 3 months before inquiring on the progress of your manuscript. Should there be no reply after this period; make use of your tracking ID to inquire on the status of your story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record the tracking number from the confirmation email. Only inquire after 5 weeks–3 months have passed, and use the tracking ID when asking about status.

rubrics_metrics.name: No reprints or simultaneous submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: A word of caution: Asimov’s does not accept reprints or simultaneous submissions. Be sure to follow those guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not submit work that has been previously published (reprints). Do not submit the same piece to multiple markets simultaneously; withdraw elsewhere before querying Asimov's.
